claims: The Artemis II crew splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego on April 10, 2026, at 8:07 p.m. ET.
The Artemis II mission lasted 10 days.
Recovery teams from the USS John P. Murtha rescued the four astronauts.
The four astronauts are in good health.
Splashdown occurred at 8:07 p.m. ET (5:07 p.m. PT) on April 10, 2026.
Splashdown location was the Pacific Ocean near San Diego, California.
Artemis II completed a crewed lunar flyby.
The spacecraft was the Orion capsule.
The recovery team was the USS John P. Murtha of the US Navy.
The Orion capsule survived a plunge through Earth's atmosphere at 39,590 km/h.
39,590 km/h is 24 times faster than a bullet.
The re-entry marked the first crewed return from the Moon since 1972.
After splashdown, the crew was extracted via helicopters from the capsule to the USS John P. Murtha within roughly two hours.
The Artemis II crew members are Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
All four crew members underwent initial medical checks on the ship before being flown back to shore.
The Artemis II crew travelled farther from Earth than anyone in human history.
Artemis II is the first crewed mission of the Artemis program.
